source.title: Forgotten Tells of Mali
source.source_family: Inland Niger Delta archaeological field surveys, 1977 and 1981
source.license: Copyright Penn Museum; no open reuse license established.

interpretation: Floodplain rice, fishing and seasonal grazing formed complementary livelihoods. Flood timing constrained farming. River commerce supplied Timbuktu from the more productive southern delta; this does not establish an import quantity for 1337. Treat existing northern-delta fields as mainly water-dependent, rather than assigning them almost entirely to zero-yield rainfed cultivation.

assignment.range_role: Inferred regional system mapping, not measured local irrigation or development. Existing field extent remains fixed. The fraction concerns those fields only, not the province's desert area.

exclusions: Do not allocate the entire delta's flooded area as cultivated land.
Do not turn every flood into controlled irrigation or add rice, fish and grazing on the same resource twice.
Do not grant extra harvests, cultivated hectares, canals or future water opportunities.
Do not infer local agricultural self-sufficiency from Timbuktu's trading population.
